title: A random line across a circle can have more than one right probability
body: Choose a chord, a straight line joining two points on a circle. The chance it is longer than the side of an inscribed equilateral triangle is one-third if you choose two points uniformly. Other ways of choosing a chord give different results.
takeaway: A probability question needs a precise rule for how the sample is drawn.
visual: a circular ring crossed by several fine straight threads

title: An infinite hotel can be full and still take another guest
body: Imagine a hotel with rooms numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on without end. Even if all rooms are occupied, moving each guest to the next room frees room 1 without leaving anyone outside.
takeaway: An infinite collection can match up with a proper subset of itself, which finite collections cannot do.
visual: a hotel corridor with identical unnumbered doors stretching into darkness

title: Thirty-six dots can make a square or a solid triangle
body: A square array with six dots on each side uses 36 dots. A triangle with rows of one, two and so on up to eight dots also uses 36. Mathematicians call this a square triangular number.
takeaway: Numbers can share two geometric patterns, even when the shapes are built in very different ways.
visual: two arrangements of small stones, one in a square and one in a filled triangle
